messages.subject: JOB: Programming (including Distance), St Andrews
parts:
Below an advert for a job with a substantial component programming the=20
software Distance. Please feel free to pass on to anyone you feel would=20
be interested and qualified. Thanks! - Len Thomas

Research Fellow in Statistical Computing
=A329,853 - =A335,646 per annum

Centre for Research into Ecological and Environmental Modelling (CREEM)
School of Mathematics and Statistics
University of St Andrews
Scotland

Closing date for applications: 24 May 2010

The post is for 1 year, with a possible extension to a further 2 years,=20
and is available from 1 July 2010, or as soon as possible thereafter.=20
You will collaborate with other research staff within the Centre for=20
Research into Ecological and Environmental Modelling (CREEM) to write,=20
test and maintain computer code to implement new statistical methods=20
developed within the centre. You may also participate in development of=20
the new methods and in writing up the research outputs for publication.=20
If desired, there is the possibility to co-teach the more=20
computational parts of some undergraduate courses.

You will work on a variety of projects. The main project involves=20
extending the software Distance, written by members of CREEM (and=20
others) to allow the design and analysis of distance sampling surveys of=20
wildlife populations. Other potential projects involve implementing=20
code in the statistical environment R to allow statistical modelling of=20
wildlife population dynamics; writing code in a 3rd generation language=20
(3GL) to model animal movement based on tag data; implementing parallel=20
processing techniques; and writing Bayesian statistical models in the=20
software OpenBUGS.

You should have training and practical experience in scientific=20
computing, and some training in statistics. You should be familiar with=20
the statistical environment R; experience of 3GLs is desirable, as is=20
experience with Visual Basic, OpenBUGS and parallel programming. Good=20
communication and team working skills are essential, and experience=20
working collaboratively within a research environment is desirable. An=20
interest in statistical ecology will be a distinct advantage.

Informal enquiries to Dr Len Thomas (email: l...@mcs.st-and.ac.uk).

Closing date for applications: 24 May 2010

Interviews will be held on 4th June 2010

Further particulars of the position are available from the university=20
recruitment web site:
https://www.vacancies.st-andrews.ac.uk/Vacancies.aspx
or directly from
http://www.creem.st-and.ac.uk/len/SK4935.pdf
